passage: Note from class teacher, Monday. During break, Varun climbed the compound wall to fetch a kite. When I called him to come down, he said, "I won't fall, I'm strong." He did not seem to think about the road on the other side, or how far the ground was. I helped him down myself, and we sat together. I asked him to tell me where he would have landed. He looked, and went quiet. We made a rule on a card: no climbing walls; if something goes over, ask a teacher. He put the card in his bag. Please repeat the rule at home. Manjula, class teacher

qa.q: What did Varun climb to fetch a kite?
qa.a: Varun climbed the compound wall to fetch a kite.

qa.q: What was Varun thinking when he said "I won't fall, I'm strong"?
qa.a: Varun felt confident and did not picture the road or the drop, so the danger was not real to him.

qa.q: What could Varun's parents do at home to support the rule?
qa.a: They could repeat the card's rule, that if something goes over he asks a grown-up, and remind him kindly whenever a ball or kite goes astray.

qa.q: How does Manjula see Varun's climbing?
qa.a: Manjula sees a child whose sense of consequences is short-range, so the teacher helps him down, asks where he would have landed and sets a clear rule.

grounding: Shows a schoolchild climbing without imagining consequences and an adult setting clear limits.

passage: Friday. Santosh bhaiya said no cycling near the main road side, but I know how to stop. So after tuition I went down the lane slope with no hands, going faster and faster. At the bottom an auto came out of the gate. I squeezed both brakes and the cycle skidded and my knee scraped on the road. The auto man shouted. My heart was going boom boom boom. I walked home holding the handlebar. Santosh bhaiya was on the steps. He did not shout. He looked at my knee, then at the road, and said, "Now you see where the auto comes from." I said sorry. New rule: cycle only in the park. Sangeeta

qa.q: What did Santosh bhaiya say about cycling?
qa.a: Santosh bhaiya said no cycling near the main road side.

qa.q: What was Sangeeta feeling after the auto came out of the gate?
qa.a: Sangeeta was frightened, with the heart going boom boom boom, and sorry about ignoring the rule.

qa.q: What choice did Sangeeta make after the scrape?
qa.a: Sangeeta said sorry and agreed to a new rule to cycle only in the park.

qa.q: How might Santosh bhaiya have felt seeing the scraped knee, and why did he not shout?
qa.a: Santosh bhaiya was probably worried and relieved it was not worse, and chose to show where the auto comes from instead of shouting.

grounding: Shows a schoolchild cycling near a road without imagining consequences and learning from a near miss with adult limits.

passage:
Class teacher's note, Class 3, Wednesday.
At lunch break today, Anjali climbed the boundary wall behind the water tank to fetch a ball. The wall is about two metres high and has broken glass on top. When I called her down, she was surprised. "But I didn't fall," she said. She truly had not imagined what could happen. Her friend Omkar was already putting one foot on the wall to follow her. I brought both down, showed them the glass, and explained the rule: balls over the wall are fetched by the peon, never by children. I have asked the office to fix a net there and will remind the class tomorrow.

qa.q: How high is the boundary wall?
qa.a: About two metres high.

qa.q: What was Anjali feeling when she was called down?
qa.a: She felt surprised and a bit puzzled, since she hadn't fallen and hadn't imagined any danger.

qa.q: What steps did the teacher take, and why are they important?
qa.a: The teacher brought both children down, showed them the glass, gave a clear rule about fetching balls, and asked for a net, because children this age need adult limits.

qa.q: How might Omkar have been affected if no adult had been watching?
qa.a: Omkar was already following her up, so Omkar might have climbed too and been cut or hurt.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a child climbing a dangerous wall without imagining the consequences, and an adult setting clear limits.

passage:
Dear Diary,
Today I got in big trouble. Me and my cousin were playing near the main road, and our cricket ball rolled across. I just ran after it. A scooter honked really loud and swerved. Farida aunty from next door screamed and grabbed my arm and pulled me back. She was shaking. I didn't even think about the scooter. I was only thinking about the ball.
Aunty told Ammi, and Ammi made a new rule: if the ball goes on the road, we leave it and call a grown-up. I said that's not fair. But at night I kept thinking about the honk and my tummy felt funny.
Vaibhav

qa.q: Who pulled Vaibhav back from the road?
qa.a: Farida aunty from next door screamed and grabbed Vaibhav's arm and pulled Vaibhav back.

qa.q: What was Vaibhav feeling at night?
qa.a: Vaibhav felt uneasy and a little scared, remembering the honk, with a funny feeling in the tummy.

qa.q: Why is Ammi's new rule a good one for a child this age?
qa.a: Children often don't picture the danger in the moment, so a clear rule to leave the ball and call a grown-up protects them.

qa.q: How was Farida aunty affected by what happened?
qa.a: Farida aunty was frightened, shaking after pulling Vaibhav back from the scooter.

grounding: A child's diary shows running into a road after a ball without imagining the danger, and an adult making a clear rule.

passage: In the village near Karnal, Nilesh, eight, found a box of matches on the kitchen shelf. He took it behind the cowshed, where the hay was stacked, and struck one to see the flame. He struck another and dropped it on a few loose straws. They caught at once. His older brother Ujjwal, fifteen, came round the corner, saw the smoke and stamped out the straw, then poured a bucket of water over it. Nilesh stood frozen. "I only wanted to see," he whispered. Ujjwal took the matches and called their father. That evening, Papa put the matchbox on a high shelf and made a rule: no fire without a grown-up, ever.

qa.q: Where was the hay stacked?
qa.a: Behind the cowshed.

qa.q: What was Nilesh feeling when he whispered "I only wanted to see"?
qa.a: He felt frightened and shocked, not having imagined that the straw would catch so quickly.

qa.q: What protective steps did the family take?
qa.a: Ujjwal put out the fire and called their father, who put the matches out of reach and set a clear rule: no fire without a grown-up.

qa.q: How might Ujjwal have felt when he saw the smoke?
qa.a: Ujjwal was probably alarmed and scared for his brother, acting fast to put out the fire.

grounding: Shows a child playing with matches without imagining the consequences, and adults setting firm limits afterwards.

passage: In the Vancouver flat, Xin built a blanket fort and wanted it to glow like a cave. She took a leftover birthday candle and the long lighter from the kitchen drawer, and set the flame on a saucer by her pillow. Then her dog pushed in, and the blanket sagged low over it. Santiago, her stepfather, smelt something hot and pulled the blanket back. The edge had a brown scorch mark. He blew out the candle. "I was watching it the whole time!" Xin said, her lip shaking. "I know you were," he said. "But you didn't see Pepper move the blanket. New rule: candles and lighters only at the kitchen table, with a grown-up. The lighter lives on the top shelf now." Xin stared at the brown mark.

qa.q: Where did Xin put the candle?
qa.a: On a saucer by her pillow.

qa.q: What was Xin feeling when Santiago pulled the blanket back?
qa.a: She was upset and defensive, insisting she was watching it, with her lip shaking, probably also scared by the scorch mark.

qa.q: What did Santiago do that fits a child of Xin's age?
qa.a: He stayed calm, explained the part she couldn't foresee, the dog moving the blanket, and set a clear rule and moved the lighter out of reach.

qa.q: How might Santiago have felt when he smelt something hot?
qa.a: He was probably frightened, but he sat down and spoke gently instead of shouting.

grounding: Shows a schoolchild who plays with fire without imagining what could go wrong, and an adult who responds with a clear rule and limits.
